title: Theaters, the Lyric and the old dance halls
summary: Elysian, Palace, Orpheum and the Lyric with its musicians, plus Storyville and the dances.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, you get tired. Oh, you have to get tired. You get tired. What were some of the big theaters here, by the way? Did you ever hear of the Elysian Theater? I used to go there. Well, that's a new one on the island.
Yeah, I just heard of it once.

Used to be right down here off of the Frenchman and, is that the one you're talking about? One off of Frenchman's Creek? Yeah. Frenchman and Elysian Field? Somewhere around. That's why it was called Elysian. Yeah. And Elysian Field runs there. Of course, you had these theaters up here in town off Iberville Street, the old palace. Mm-hmm. And you had the Orpheum. Is that still going? The Orpheum?
Yeah. It's still going. But the palace is gone. It's not quite the same thing. But the palace is gone. The palace is gone.
And then there was the Negro Theatre, the Lyric.
Well, that was a melting pot for some of the great musicians. Mm-hmm. There was a left-hand violin player there. I can't recall his name. John Robichaud. No, no.
Val Coo. Val Coo? Mr. Val Coo. I've heard of Val Toe. Val Toe. Yeah.
Val Toe. It's either Val Coo or Val Toe.
But then you also had these great drummers that like Red Happy. But he was an import. He wasn't originally from here.

I think he came from Memphis. But this guy was a trick drummer. Oh yeah. And of course you had old man Cottrell that was strictly a drummer. He was a Finnish musician drummer. Of course my daddy knew these people and he was real close friends with them. And he used to tell me. And I met them and I knew them. They knew me real well. I was just a kid. But the friendship always is beautiful.
What about the View of Korea in those days at Bourbon Street and all that? When did Bourbon Street start booming? Do you remember?

No, I sure can't dig. There was nothing when you were a kid? No, sure you had a lot of these. That's where the, well as they say the Hattons was. Plus Storyville, which was the, where Lula White and all this was. Yeah. But the joints were still there because you can look at the old Absinthe House and see how old that thing is. Yeah. So that's part of it.
There were some joints anywhere in the Bourbon Street. Sure there were some joints.
In the old days the big thing though were the balls, the dances at the Franz Ami Hall. And each section there. And then you had this San Su uptown and different places like that. Mostly dances.
